key_insight: lPINN shifts most neural training offline by pretraining nonlinear basis functions, then solves new differential-equation instances online with only a frozen linear layer and physics residual minimization.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed modeling faster and more scalable for forward and inverse PDE/ODE problems while preserving differentiability and cross-resolution evaluation.
method: Learn continuous neural basis functions offline from an ensemble of numerical solutions.
Pretrain the hidden representation with solution data plus derivatives or physics residuals.
Freeze the basis online and fit only the final linear coefficients using governing-equation, boundary, initial, and data constraints.
evidence_signal: The paper reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors and about 1 to more than 100× faster online inference than vanilla PINNs, especially with limited residual or measurement data.
watch_item: The approach depends on a representative offline ensemble and careful pretraining so the learned basis generalizes to new parameter regimes and mesh resolutions.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
